tickets.title: Running Account Ledger Balances
tickets.description: Accumulates transaction history to show running passbook totals for Account 1.
tasks: Accumulates transaction history to show running passbook totals for Account 1.
learning_objectives: Understand relational database design and PostgreSQL features.
tickets.evaluation: `compare_result_set(actual, expected)` `check_command_used("SUM")` `check_command_used("OVER")` **[A] Correctness (40 pts)**: 40 pts for correct running cumulative values. **[B] Optimality (30 pts)**: 30 pts if status check is optimized. **[C] Quality (20 pts)**: 20 pts for bounded partition windows.
common_mistakes: Forgetting semicolons at the end of statements.
Using reserved keywords as column names without quotes.
hints: Remember to use GROUP BY for aggregate functions like SUM, COUNT, or AVG.

solution.query.sql:
SELECT
      id AS transaction_id,
      amount,
      status,
      created_at,
      SUM(amount) OVER (ORDER BY created_at ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) AS running_balance
    FROM transactions
    WHERE account_id = 1;

tickets.title: Velocity Risk checks (LAG / LEAD)
tickets.description: Detects rapid consecutive transactions (transfers made within 60 seconds of the previous transaction on the same account).
tasks: Detects rapid consecutive transactions (transfers made within 60 seconds of the previous transaction on the same account).
learning_objectives: Understand relational database design and PostgreSQL features.
tickets.evaluation: `compare_result_set(actual, expected)` `check_command_used("LAG")` `check_command_used("EXTRACT")` **[A] Correctness (40 pts)**: 40 pts for identifying consecutive swift entries. **[B] Optimality (30 pts)**: 30 pts for utilizing timestamp subtractions. **[C] Quality (20 pts)**: 20 pts for selecting explicit elapsed ranges.
common_mistakes: Forgetting semicolons at the end of statements.
Using reserved keywords as column names without quotes.
hints: Remember to use GROUP BY for aggregate functions like SUM, COUNT, or AVG.

solution.query.sql:
WITH tx_lag AS (
      SELECT
        id,
        account_id,
        created_at,
        LAG(created_at) OVER (PARTITION BY account_id ORDER BY created_at) AS prev_tx_time
      FROM transactions
    )
    SELECT id, account_id, created_at, prev_tx_time
    FROM tx_lag
    WHERE prev_tx_time IS NOT NULL AND EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (created_at - prev_tx_time)) <= 60;
